title: Towards a Unified View of Preference Learning for Large Language Models: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying literature and meta-evaluation benchmarks (e.g., FairEval) that test LLM evaluators by altering the order of candidate answers in pairwise comparisons to see if the evaluation results are hacked or changed.
Reviewing studies that evaluate LLM judges' tendency to inherently prefer longer outputs (surface quality) and discussing proposed debiasing metrics such as length-controlled win rates.
Reviewing existing research that analyzes whether LLM-based evaluators show a predisposition to favor outputs generated by models similar to themselves.
